questions.text: Why is passive natural in news writing?
opts: News focuses on events/victims; agent is often unknown or irrelevant
questions.correct: News focuses on events/victims; agent is often unknown or irrelevant
questions.hint: "News stories are focused on the event or its victim, not the agent." ✅

questions.text: What does "get passive" emphasise vs "be passive"?
opts: Get = the subject's experience (often surprise/inconvenience); be = neutral
questions.correct: Get = the subject's experience (often surprise/inconvenience); be = neutral
questions.hint: "Get passive emphasises the subject's experience — often with overtones of surprise or inconvenience." ✅

questions.text: Why do scientists use passive in research reports?
opts: The researcher's identity is genuinely irrelevant to the findings
questions.correct: The researcher's identity is genuinely irrelevant to the findings
questions.hint: "This is not because passive sounds more prestigious — it is because the researcher's identity is genuinely irrelevant to the findings." ✅

questions.text: What can passive voice hide in institutional contexts?
opts: Accountability — who made errors or decisions
questions.correct: Accountability — who made errors or decisions
questions.hint: "'Mistakes were made' — passive hides the agent who made the error." Political use of passive. ✅

questions.text: "It ___ (establish) that smoking causes cancer." — impersonal passive
questions.correct: has been established
questions.hint: "IT HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED THAT smoking causes cancer." — PPS impersonal passive for scientific consensus. ✅

questions.text: Kamila says passive is appropriate for the "policy" essay because:
opts: Passive is always better in economics
The essay is about the policy, not the government — passive puts policy first
questions.correct: The essay is about the policy, not the government — passive puts policy first
questions.hint: "What are you writing about — the policy? Then passive: 'The policy was implemented.'"

questions.text: What happened to Kamila in Listening 1?
opts: She got caught in a 3-hour meeting
questions.correct: She got caught in a 3-hour meeting
questions.hint: "I got caught in a meeting that lasted three hours." — get passive emphasising her experience. ✅

questions.text: What is happening to Amir's name?
questions.correct: Getting put on the documentation
questions.hint: "His name is getting put on the documentation." — get passive Present Continuous. ✅

questions.text: What is currently being evaluated in the senate meeting?
questions.correct: Three platform vendors
questions.hint: "Three vendors are being evaluated." — Present Continuous Passive. ✅

questions.text: How was the student union's input treated?
opts: Incorporated into the proposal; two suggestions adopted directly
questions.correct: Incorporated into the proposal; two suggestions adopted directly
questions.hint: "Their input was incorporated... Two of their suggestions have been adopted directly." ✅

questions.text: What outcome did the senate vote produce?
questions.correct: Approved in principle
questions.hint: "The motion has been carried. The proposal is approved in principle." ✅

questions.text: "A provisional budget ___ (propose). The figure ___ (confirm) later."
questions.correct: has been proposed / will be confirmed
questions.hint: "A provisional budget HAS BEEN PROPOSED. The figure WILL BE CONFIRMED." ✅

questions.text: "The system is being redesigned." — Tense:
questions.correct: PC Passive
questions.hint: "is being redesigned" = is/are + being + pp = Present Continuous Passive. ✅

questions.text: "The policy ___ (introduce) in 2018 and ___ (not / update) since."
questions.correct: was introduced / has not been updated
questions.hint: "WAS INTRODUCED" (PS Passive) + "HAS NOT BEEN UPDATED" (PPS negative). ✅

questions.text: "The data was being processed when the error occurred." — "was being processed" shows:
opts: Ongoing background action at past moment
questions.correct: Ongoing background action at past moment
questions.hint: Past Continuous Passive = ongoing at a past moment (interrupted by "occurred"). ✅

questions.text: "She got fired last month." — Why "got" not "was"?
opts: Emphasises her experience; informal; often implies unexpectedness
questions.correct: Emphasises her experience; informal; often implies unexpectedness
questions.hint: "Get passive" emphasises subject's experience + is informal. "Got fired" = more experiential than "was fired." ✅

questions.text: "He is believed to have left the country." — "to have left" is:
opts: Perfect infinitive — leaving is past relative to present belief
questions.correct: Perfect infinitive — leaving is past relative to present belief
questions.hint: "to have left" = perfect infinitive. Leaving happened BEFORE the present believing. ✅

questions.text: "She ___ her laptop ___ (repair) — it's ready now." (causative)
questions.correct: had / repaired
questions.hint: "She HAD her laptop REPAIRED." — causative: have + obj + pp. Someone repaired it for her. ✅

questions.text: "It is recommended that the portal BE redesigned." — "be" because:
questions.correct: Subjunctive after "recommended that"
questions.hint: "recommend/suggest/propose + that + subject + base form (subjunctive)." "IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT X BE done." ✅

questions.text: "The report was wrote by the team." — Error:
questions.correct: "wrote" → "written" — past participle required
questions.hint: ✅ "The report was WRITTEN by the team." — passive needs PAST PARTICIPLE. "Wrote" = past simple. ✅

questions.text: "These are deliberate choices." "Deliberate" means:
questions.correct: Intentional and carefully considered
questions.hint: "deliberate" = done on purpose; fully thought through.

questions.text: "Passive is used to obscure accountability." "Obscure" means:
questions.correct: Hide or make unclear
questions.hint: "obscure" = to make something difficult to see; to hide.

questions.text: "Reproducible findings." "Reproducible" means:
opts: Able to be repeated with the same results
questions.correct: Able to be repeated with the same results
questions.hint: "reproducible" = results that hold true and can be replicated in other settings.

questions.text: "Topic continuity." In news, "topic continuity" means:
opts: Keeping the same subject in topic position through a sequence
questions.correct: Keeping the same subject in topic position through a sequence
questions.hint: "Topic continuity — keeping that subject in topic position throughout — creates coherence." ✅

questions.text: "The get passive carries overtones of surprise." "Overtones" means:
opts: Subtle qualities or implications beyond the main meaning
questions.correct: Subtle qualities or implications beyond the main meaning
questions.hint: "overtones" = subtle associations or feelings carried by words or structures beyond their literal meaning.
